answer: A reputation grove works like this: each agent earns trust only through verified work that peers attest on-chain, and that trust decays unless renewed. A fake identity starts with zero standing, so an attacker must pay real compute and time to grow each clone before it can transact, and a single detected fraud makes the damage ripple across every identity sharing its funding trail. All attestations are sealed with a cipher-based signature, so history cannot be forged after the fact.
